solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spoke to accountant about business started without talent

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the accountant's letters run backwards

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: without means the talent is taken out of the word started

parts.note: art is a talent or skill

explanation.surface: Someone addressed an accountant about a firm founded with no flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns CA round; 'without' removes ART from STARTED. 'Spoke to' is the definition, not a verb about wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and speak to them, often boldly.

clue.text: Alcohol free wine at last in cellar

indicators.note: free signals the letters are freed up and rearranged
at last means the final letter of wine

explanation.surface: A cellar with no booze in it and only wine at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges ALCOHOL plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalhole is a cellar or compartment for storing coal.

clue.text: Music expert has speaker placed round front of royal box

indicators.note: placed round means the speaker goes around the other letters

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
a chest is a box

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of royal

explanation.surface: A music specialist has a loudspeaker set around the royal box at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed round' wraps the speaker around the box plus R; the royal box suggests a theatre, but box is just CHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestrator arranges music for the instruments of an orchestra.

clue.text: Giant bird going over a loch

indicators.note: going over means in this down clue the bird sits above the rest

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: A huge bird flying over a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A titaness is a female Titan, one of the giant deities of Greek myth.

clue.text: Democrat attracted to left, after unusually favouring the right?

indicators.note: after sends the word for left behind the word meaning unusually

parts.note: extra means unusually, as in extra large

explanation.surface: A Democrat drawn to the left, then oddly leaning right politically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' looks like an anagram signal, but here it means EXTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextral means right-handed, or turned towards the right side.

clue.text: Gala's, perhaps, not broadcast

definitions.meaning: a gala is a fair, so of a fair, the phrase split as two words
describes a programme or remark not transmitted

explanation.surface: A festival's coverage is cut from the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as OF FAIR, the phrase means belonging to a fair, such as a gala.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-air describes what happens when a station is not transmitting.

clue.text: Vehicle: auto oddly turning over on side

indicators.note: turning over means the odd letters are turned upside down in this down clue
oddly means the first and third letters of auto

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: A car flipping over onto its side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks AT from auto and 'turning over' makes it TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a car for hire, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Fit after gym session's ending? Not if this colour!

indicators.note: after places the word for fit behind the gym letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym
to agree is to fit or match

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of session

explanation.surface: Feeling fit after a gym session? Not if you've gone green!
explanation.walkthrough: The unfit go green in the face after exercise, hence 'Not if'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea-green is a bright yellowish-green shade, like garden peas.

clue.text: In French field, a strange position for troops

parts.note: the French word for in is en

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of field and a are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: In a French field, troops are placed in an odd spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges FIELD and A into FILADE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfilade is a military position letting troops fire along the length of an enemy line.

clue.text: Brandy butter sent back cold

indicators.note: sent back means the butter's letters are returned, read backwards

parts.note: a ram is a butter, an animal that butts
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Brandy butter being returned because it is cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one that butts, a RAM; 'sent back' makes it MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a brandy distilled from the grape pulp left after wine pressing.

clue.text: Encouraging ambassador, fighting dynasty, to bring in resistance

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: to bring in means the phrase for fighting takes the resistance letter inside it

parts.note: at war means fighting
R is the physics symbol for resistance
the Ming was a Chinese dynasty

explanation.surface: An envoy is cheered by a warring dynasty showing some resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring in' places R inside AT WAR to give ARTWAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartwarming lifts the spirits and gives emotional encouragement.

clue.text: French teacher devised way of working, I understand, accommodating learners

parts.note: made means devised
MO, modus operandi, is a way of working

indicators.note: accommodating means the phrase for understanding holds the learners

parts.note: I see means I understand
L is a learner, from the L-plate, so two learners are LL

explanation.surface: A French teacher devised a teaching method that suits pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts LL inside I SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools the French teacher was traditionally addressed as Mademoiselle.

clue.text: Swimwear is rejected by English on Greek island

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

indicators.note: rejected means the word is is turned back on itself

explanation.surface: Swimwear is spurned by an English visitor on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' signals the turnaround; the answer is informal British and Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossie is a colloquial shortening of swimming costume, a bathing suit.

clue.text: Terrier given outing by chap, without lead

parts.note: to be aired is to be given an outing

indicators.note: without lead means the first letter is lost

parts.note: a chap is a male

explanation.surface: A terrier is taken for a walk by a man, no lead attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without lead' reads like a dog off its leash, but it drops the M of MALE, leaving ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large breed of terrier from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Check on news media

parts.note: re means on or concerning
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: A look at what the papers and broadcasters are up to.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to check or hold back, as with feelings.

clue.text: Right to payment from engineering lessons?

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the army's engineering corps
a course is a series of lessons

explanation.surface: A claim for fees from an engineering course.
explanation.definitionFit: In law and finance, recourse is the right to demand payment from someone.

clue.text: Description of a war cry, short, to be precise

indicators.note: short means the word cry is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: I mean is a phrase used to be precise

explanation.surface: A battle cry, briefly put, to be exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimean is the adjective used of the 1850s war fought in the Crimea.

clue.text: Reggae fans roused by punk

indicators.note: punk, meaning rough or worthless, signals the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Reggae fans are stirred up by a punk band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punk' rearranges ROUSED BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude boys were Jamaican youth subculture followers of ska and reggae.

clue.text: One Catholic leader's answer, definitely not accepting advice

indicators.note: accepting means the strong refusal takes the advice inside it

parts.note: nope means definitely not
a tip is advice

explanation.surface: A Catholic leader's reply is a flat refusal to take advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' signals the insertion; the 's after leader is a link, read as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: An antipope is a rival claimant to the papacy, set up against the elected pope.

clue.text: Precious bank's less generous

parts.note: pet means precious, beloved
a tier is a bank, as of seats

explanation.surface: A beloved bank is becoming stingier.
explanation.definitionFit: Pettier means more petty, smaller-minded and so meaner.

clue.text: At length home covered by revolutionary telephone service

indicators.note: covered by means the other pieces sit inside the revolutionary

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
in means at home

explanation.surface: A long stay at home under a revolutionary, with only the phone for company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' puts ATLIN inside CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatline is a phone service where callers talk to each other or to paid hosts.

clue.text: Outer London town I regularly left, taking ring road

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of left

parts.note: O is a ring by its shape

explanation.surface: I left town on a ring road, as one does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes LF from left; Ilford is a town in east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilford is a town in the London Borough of Redbridge, on the city's eastern edge.

clue.text: Doctor daily jabs one's veins

indicators.note: jabs means the daily paper pokes into the other piece

parts.note: one's is read as I is, I being one
the FT, the Financial Times, is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A doctor giving daily injections into someone's veins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jabs' signals the insertion; a 'daily' in crosswords is a newspaper, and veins are the mining sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In mining, a drift is a horizontal passage cut along a vein of ore, and also a deposit of it.

clue.text: Vain academic engaged by university board

indicators.note: engaged by means the academic is held within the university

parts.note: a prof is a professor, an academic
a table is a board

explanation.surface: A conceited don is hired by a university's governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' looks like conceited, but it means fruitless; 'engaged by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain effort is futile, and an unprofitable one brings no gain.

clue.text: Former pacifist's quarters on the outskirts

indicators.note: quarters on the outskirts means only the two outer quarters of the word pacifist are kept

parts.note: the word pacifist taken as written, its possessive ending ignored

explanation.surface: An ex-pacifist living in the suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: PACIFIST has eight letters; its first and last quarters are PA and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Past and former both describe something that has gone before.

clue.text: Diver in lake having nothing on

parts.note: O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Someone diving into a lake without a stitch on.
explanation.definitionFit: The loon, called a diver in Britain, is a bird that dives for fish.

clue.text: Coin once passed round in secret session

indicators.note: passed round means the hidden letters run backwards
in means the answer lies within the words secret session

explanation.surface: An old coin is handed around during a closed meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'secret session' backwards and the coin appears in the middle: noisSESTERCEs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sesterce was a small Roman silver coin, so currency of times past.

clue.text: Healthy-sounding vegetable chopped for tea

indicators.note: sounding means the word for healthy is spoken, giving a name said the same

parts.note: rosy means healthy-looking

indicators.note: chopped means the vegetable loses its last letter

parts.note: a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A wholesome vegetable is cut up for the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSIE LEE is Cockney rhyming slang for tea; 'Healthy-sounding' gives ROSIE, said like ROSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie Lee is rhyming slang, from London's East End, for a cup of tea.
